subtopic: Class A, B, and C Shares
source_evidence: Class A shares might have a front-end sales load paid as a percentage of the purchase price... Class C shares might have a 12b-1 fee and a contingent deferred sales load (CDSL)... Class B shares with a CDSL and a higher 12b-1 fee, but no front-end sales load were once relatively common. However, Class B shares are no longer widely available.
question: How do Class A, B, and C shares commonly differ in their sales charges and ongoing fees?
answer: Class A shares may have a front-end sales load and generally have a lower 12b-1 fee than certain other load-bearing classes. Class B shares traditionally had no front-end sales load but had a contingent deferred sales load (CDSL) and a higher 12b-1 fee; they are no longer widely available. Class C shares may have a 12b-1 fee and a CDSL for some period, and their 12b-1 fee is generally higher than that of other load-bearing classes. These are common features, not guarantees for every fund, so compare the specific share-class fees and expenses.
